`final class UIView`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.ui.core.view` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [UIView.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/ui/core/view/UIView.java)

Converts between the screen pixels of the window and the design pixels of a UI, from the window size, the anchor, the interface scale and the zoom.

## Description

Every [`UI`](/reference/ui/ui/) has one view, returned by [`UI.getView`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-getView).
The view fits the 1920 × 1080 design canvas in the window without cropping it, then applies the interface scale and the zoom around the anchor.
Use it to place your own drawing in screen pixels or to read where the window edges fall on the canvas.

## Learn more

- [The design canvas](/use/learn/describing-the-ui/design-canvas/)

## Creation details

<a id="UIView-factory-create"></a>

### create

`UIView create(double anchorX, double anchorY)` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

Creates a view whose anchor is this point of the design canvas, for a 1920 × 1080 window, with no zoom and no interface scale.
A UI creates its own view from its anchors.

## Property details

<a id="UIView-property-anchorX"></a>

### anchorX

- `this anchorX(double anchorX)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `double getAnchorX()` 

**Default:** set at creation

Horizontal position, in design pixels, of the anchor that the canvas zooms around and stays pinned to when the window shows more than the canvas.

<a id="UIView-property-anchorY"></a>

### anchorY

- `this anchorY(double anchorY)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `double getAnchorY()` 

**Default:** set at creation

Vertical position, in design pixels, of the anchor that the canvas zooms around and stays pinned to.

<a id="UIView-property-zoom"></a>

### zoom

- `this zoom(double zoom)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `double getZoom()` 

**Default:** `1D`

Zoom applied on top of the interface scale.
The view keeps the value asked for, even beyond the bounds, and `getZoom()` returns it kept within `clampZoom`; unlike [`UI.zoom(double)`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-zoom), writing it here runs no listener.

<a id="UIView-property-interfaceScale"></a>

### interfaceScale

- `this interfaceScale(double interfaceScale)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `double getInterfaceScale()` 

**Default:** `1D`

Factor that the UI bridge applies to make every UI larger or smaller, after the `@UIDataScale` of the UI.

<a id="UIView-method-getRequestedZoom"></a>

### getRequestedZoom

`double getRequestedZoom()` 

Returns the zoom asked for, before the bounds of `clampZoom`, by `UI.zoom(...)` or by `zoom(...)` of the view.
A value written to the view that equals the zoom shown keeps a request of `UI.zoom(...)` for the next change of interface scale, while `getRequestedZoom()` returns the value written.

### clampZoom

`double clampZoom(double zoom)`

<a id="UIView-method-resize"></a>

### resize

`this resize(double width, double height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Fits the view to a window of this size, in screen pixels.
A size of `0` or below, such as a minimized window, is ignored.

<a id="UIView-method-render"></a>

### render

`void render(IRenderBridge render, boolean projection, Runnable draw)` 

Runs the drawing in the coordinates of the design canvas.
If `projection` is `true`, it also sets an orthographic projection on the viewport; if `false`, it keeps the projection of the caller and applies only the offset, the scale and the zoom.
